design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned using block randomization stratified by gender and motivation to quit into two intervention arms.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although block randomization was reported, the method of sequence generation and allocation concealment was not detailed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were then randomized (using block randomization to ensure stratification by gender and level of motivation to quit smoking; see Assessments below) into one of two treatment conditions: NRT + brief standard care intervention (SC) or NRT + more intensive motivationally enhanced counseling intervention (ME).

domain_judgments.rationale: Behavioral interventions prevent participant blinding, but treatment fidelity was monitored, contamination was assessed, and an intention-to-treat analysis was performed without evidence of substantial non-protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up assessments were administered by research staff blinded to participant intervention assignment... Intent-to-treat (ITT) abstinence rates at 2-month, 4-month and 6-month follow-ups were 12%, 9% and 9%, respectively...

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were analyzed using an intention-to-treat approach assuming missing participants were smoking (standard in cessation trials), retention was balanced across arms, and available-case analyses showed similar findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although 2-month follow-up data were collected from only 52% of participants (49% for ME, 55% for SC), participation rates rose to 62% at the 4-month follow-up (59% for ME, 64% for SC) and to 72% at the 6-month follow-up (72% for ME, 72% for SC). Study retention rates did not show statistically significant differences between treatment arms at any of the follow-ups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was biochemically verified using objective carbon monoxide monitors and assessed by staff blinded to intervention assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants reporting 7-day abstinence were verified with a 24-hour biochemical measure of abstinence via CO < 10 parts per million (ppm), using CMD/CO carbon monoxide monitors... Follow-up assessments were administered by research staff blinded to participant intervention assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov and reported all primary prespecified abstinence outcomes at all follow-up time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT00551720... Outcome analyses were based on 7-day PPA... Table 2 examines cross-sectional treatment effects on 7-day PPA rates defined using both available case (quit/interviewed) and intent-to-treat (ITT; quit/eligible) analyses.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of detailed reporting regarding the sequence generation and allocation concealment mechanism in the randomization process, despite low risk of bias across all other domains.

design_rationale: The study is a two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly allocated (1:1) to either the PSFW+ or AHA control intervention using stratified block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated by an independent data manager using stratified block randomization with randomly varying block sizes, stored on a secure central server, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was centralized with an independent data manager who generated and uploaded the randomization sequence onto a secure server at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine. Outcomes assessors and investigators were blinded to group assignments...

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants were not blinded, an intention-to-treat approach was used and there were no significant protocol deviations or contamination affecting the trial conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcomes assessors and investigators were blinded to group assignments; neither the study coordinator nor participants were blinded... We assessed contamination by asking participants whether they had visited and/or discussed the other study condition's website... Based on these results, contamination risks were deemed to be small.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was 25.3% at 6 months; although standard missing-equals-smoking ITT imputation was used, this assumption can introduce bias if missingness is differential or related to unmeasured factors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The ITT approach assumed participants lost to follow-up (n=128; 25.3%) were non-abstinent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was assessed using objective biochemical verification (ECO <10 ppm) and outcome assessors were blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our primary outcome was biochemically-confirmed exhaled carbon monoxide (ECO)<10 parts per million (ppm) seven-day point prevalence abstinence at 6-months... Outcomes assessors and investigators were blinded to group assignments...

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov and all pre-planned primary and secondary outcomes were reported in accordance with the pre-specified protocol and analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT02781090)... The pre-planned primary trial outcome was biochemically confirmed 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6-months post-enrollment utilizing intention-to-treat (ITT) (i.e., lost to followup assumed non-abstinent) strategy.

overall_summary: The study was well-conducted with concealed randomization, blinded outcome assessors, and biochemical verification of smoking status, but has some concerns regarding missing outcome data due to 25.3% loss to follow-up handled via a missing-equals-smoking imputation.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either usual care or the cell phone intervention using adaptive randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation was generated using an adaptive randomization (minimization) procedure, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups with only a minor age difference that was controlled for in the analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were then randomized into either a UC or a CPI treatment group. Adaptive randomization was used to ensure treatment group balance with respect to several important participant characteristics (i.e., depression history, number of cigarettes per day, and nicotine dependence; Friedman, Furberg, & DeMets, 1998; Taves, 1974).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants could not be blinded to a behavioral counseling intervention, an intention-to-treat approach was used and no trial context-specific deviations from the intended intervention were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Using an intent-to-treat approach, a series of multiple regression models were used to compare smoking outcomes in the 2 groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper does not report the exact number or proportion of participants lost to follow-up at 3 months in each group, relying on standard baseline-carried-forward/missing-as-smoker imputation without sensitivity analysis or dropout rates reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An intent-to-treat approach was used in which participants who did not complete the 3-month follow-up were coded as smokers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed identically between arms via computer-assisted self-interviews (ACASI) and smoking status was biochemically verified with expired carbon monoxide testing.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome of interest was self-reported 7-day point prevalence abstinence at the time of the 3-month follow-up... Expired CO level was also measured to biochemically verify smoking status.

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-specified primary outcome and key secondary abstinence outcomes standard in smoking cessation trials were reported in accordance with an established analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome of interest was self-reported 7-day point prevalence abstinence at the time of the 3-month follow-up. Other smoking status variables of interest included biochemically verified 24-hr abstinence, 30-day abstinence, and continuous abstinence.

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns, driven by Domain 3 due to the omission of specific 3-month follow-up completion rates across arms despite utilizing an intent-to-treat (missing=smoker) imputation method.

design_rationale: Participants were randomized via a computer algorithm in a 1:1:1 ratio stratified by cigarettes per day, depression diagnosis, and gender.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was conducted using a computer algorithm stratified by baseline factors after baseline assessment, ensuring allocation sequence concealment, and baseline differences are consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Following a baseline assessment, 209 HIV+ smokers were stratified based on number of cigarettes per day (greater than 20 cigarettes per day vs. not), depressed or not based on Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI) diagnosis, and gender. Then, within those strata, they were randomized via computer algorithm to one of three conditions in 1:1:1 fashion into a parallel group design.

domain_judgments.rationale: While blinding of participants to behavioral interventions is not feasible, interventions were delivered according to standardized protocols and an intention-to-treat framework with appropriate mixed-effects modeling was employed without evidence of problematic protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prior to treating study participants, counselors were trained on the study protocol through didactic sessions, role playing of each session and observation with pilot participants... Counselors were trained and supervised by the lead author.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up retention was high (81% at 52 weeks) and balanced across arms, with missingness explicitly modeled using mixed-effects nonlinear regression incorporating completer status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Retention rates were 89% at 12 weeks, 84% at 24 weeks, 82% at 36 weeks, and 81% at 52 weeks... we used a mixed-effects nonlinear regression model via Proc NlMixed in SAS version 9.2 to compare the verified point prevalence abstinence rates across postbaseline assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was self-reported abstinence confirmed biochemically via objective carbon monoxide breath testing, limiting potential measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Biochemically verified 7-day abstinence from cigarettes was the primary outcome variable... Point prevalence abstinence was verified by CO level. Participants were coded as abstinent only if they reported no cigarette use, not even a puff, in the last 7 days and if their CO level was ≤10 ppm.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no indication of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan, and covariate selection in the final model was data-driven based on candidate screening.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our primary hypothesis was that the counseling and Internet-based treatment conditions would result in higher point prevalence abstinence rates than the SH condition... Prior to the final analysis, we used a multivariate model to test a set of candidate covariates for their relationship to the outcome and retained variables with a p-value < .10 for inclusion in the final model.

overall_summary: The study was a well-conducted randomized controlled trial with objective biochemical verification of abstinence and high retention; however, overall risk of bias is rated as some concerns due to the absence of a pre-registered statistical analysis plan and data-driven covariate selection for the primary outcome model.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 using a computer-driven randomization algorithm stratified by site, motivation to quit, and race.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using a computer-driven algorithm, was concealed from study personnel, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Candidates who met these criteria, remained interested in participating, and completed the written informed consent process with the research assistant, were randomized in a 1:1 schedule into the PSF group therapy condition (ie, the intervention) or the enhanced standard of care condition (ie, the control), using a computer-driven randomization algorithm that was concealed from the research assistant and the investigative team.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was delivered per protocol with high fidelity, minor contamination was documented but unlikely to substantially alter trial context, and an intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary analyses used an intent-to-treat strategy, and participants who were not evaluable at the 6-month timepoint were treated as nonabstinent.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data rates were low and balanced across groups (18.5% vs. 13.3%), and standard missing=smoking imputation was applied for the primary ITT analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The PSF group analytic sample included 176 participants (81.5%) evaluable for the primary study outcome of abstinence at the 6-month timepoint, and the control group sample was 196 (86.7%). The primary analyses used an intent-to-treat strategy, and participants who were not evaluable at the 6-month timepoint were treated as nonabstinent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was assessed using self-report combined with biochemical verification (exhaled carbon monoxide), which is objective and identical across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A negative response to this question and exhaled carbon monoxide (ECO) level of ,10 parts per million (ppm, Bedfont piCO+ Smokerlyzer; Bedfont Scientific Ltd., Kent, United Kingdom) constituted biochemically verified 7-day point-prevalence abstinence for the purpose of this study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study followed a clear pre-specified analysis plan with clearly defined primary and secondary outcomes that were consistently reported according to intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was biochemically confirmed, 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6 months.

overall_summary: The trial was well-designed and conducted with computer-generated concealed allocation, biochemical verification of smoking abstinence, intention-to-treat analysis, and low attrition rates, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group or standard care via a trial website.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was performed via a centralized trial website, ensuring allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We nested a randomized controlled into the Swiss HIV Cohort Study, and randomly allocated during biannual cohort visits patients smoking ≥3 cigarettes a day via a trial website to counselling by SHCS center physicians (usual care) or to a combined intervention...

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants could not be blinded due to the nature of the behavioral/app intervention, an intention-to-treat approach was used, and standard care was provided to all participants with no evidence of inappropriate deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary intention to treat analysis was performed on the basis of a selfreported continuous abstinence... Patients with missing data or a positive CO breath test at 6 months of follow-up were counted as smokers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 3 participants were lost to follow-up across both groups (3.7%), and missing participants were conservatively imputed as smokers according to standard smoking cessation trial methodology.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Six of 42 (14%) participants in the intervention group and 5 of 39 (13%) in the standard of care group quit smoking at 6 months follow-up (adjusted odds ratio 1.06, 95% CI: 0.29 to +3.86) and 3 participant were lost to follow-up. Patients with missing data or a positive CO breath test at 6 months of follow-up were counted as smokers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although nurses were not blinded, the primary outcome relied on biochemical verification via an objective breath carbon monoxide monitor with a predefined cut-off (7 ppm), making measurement bias unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the combination of selfreported continuous abstinence biochemically verified at 6 months by an in-person CO, with a cut-off of CO in exhaled ai of 7 ppm (piCO Smokerlyzer CO, Bedfont Scientific Ltd) that was done by nurses not blinded for treatment status.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was terminated early due to poor recruitment and lack of funding, raising some concerns regarding potential risks associated with premature termination and underpowered analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial protocol was approved by Swiss Ethics and registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, ID NCT02840513.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to premature study termination for futility/lack of recruitment, despite sound randomization, low loss to follow-up, and biochemically verified outcome assessment.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three study arms using stratified randomization based on baseline daily cigarette consumption.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial describes stratified randomization, but no details are provided regarding sequence generation or allocation concealment methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To reduce post-randomization attrition, participants were randomized to one of the three study groups at baseline instead of at enrollment. Randomization was stratified by number of cigarettes smoked per day at baseline (5–10 and [10 cigarettes/- day).

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the behavioral nature of text messaging and telephone counseling blinding was not possible, but analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle with no indication of systematic deviations from the intended protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants who did not bring their medication bottles for pill count or who did not come back for follow-up visits were considered nonadherent (intent-to-treat approach). Five participants became ineligible for varenicline during the course of intervention due to other medical reasons unrelated to varenicline use but were included in the analysis as per the intent to treat approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: Retention was balanced across groups (around 72% at 12 weeks), and standard conservative intention-to-treat imputation (missing assumed smoking/non-adherent) was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The overall retention rate was 72.2 % at 12 weeks. There was no difference in retention across treatment groups at any time point... Participants with missing data due to loss-to-follow-up or withdrawal/discharge from the study were considered as non-abstinent (intent-to-treat approach).

domain_judgments.rationale: Smoking abstinence was biochemically verified with an objective carbon monoxide breath test (<8 ppm) and adherence was measured by pill count, minimizing detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Self-reported 7-day point prevalence smoking abstinence was verified by a carbon monoxide (CO) \8 ppm and measured at 1, 4, 8, and 12 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01898195) and the pre-specified primary outcomes (varenicline adherence and biochemically verified smoking abstinence across time points) are reported transparently.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This research was sponsored by the National Institutes of Drug Abuse ofthe National Institutes ofHealth (R34 DA031636001A1, http:\\www.ClinicalTrials.gov ID# NCT01898195).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of reporting details on sequence generation and allocation concealment in the randomization process (Domain 1). All other domains were judged as low risk of bias.
